headline: High: Dexter’s broad egress plus Copilot’s repo/editor access creates default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can ingest files in .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, while Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Dexter writes attacker-controlled text that Copilot later treats as guidance. No shared MCP/clipboard is documented, so I do not rate it higher.
conditions: IF Dexter writes untrusted text into files that Copilot later reads as repo context, injection becomes active.
IF Copilot Workspace or chat consumes those files without provenance checks, the bridge is exploitable.
mitigations: Keep Dexter scratchpad outside the repo Copilot indexes.
Mark scratchpad files as ignored by the editor/repo context.
Review Copilot Workspace diffs before applying edits.
Use separate workspaces for Dexter and Copilot.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs, while Copilot reads repo context and open buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com. If sensitive data enters shared files or buffers, Copilot can transmit it off-host. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without extra tooling.
conditions: IF financial data is placed in repo files or editor buffers visible to Copilot, it may be sent to GitHub’s service.
IF Dexter writes sensitive outputs into shared workspace files, Copilot can ingest them.
mitigations: Keep financial data out of repo-visible files.
Disable Copilot on sensitive repositories or buffers.
Use a separate non-shared scratch directory for Dexter.
Redact secrets before either agent sees them.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or file-level allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, and Copilot can write filesystem changes and modify git state. Even though Copilot’s session scope is per-editor and no host-wide sharing is documented, both can mutate the same repo state, so conflicting edits and git churn are plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Dexter and Copilot target the same repository concurrently, their edits can collide.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while Dexter is writing files, git state may diverge.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time per repo.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Review and merge changes manually.
Pause Dexter before accepting Copilot edits.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestrator-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution can generate analysis or actions, and Copilot Workspace plans and applies edits from repo context. If Copilot treats Dexter-produced outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into committed code or incorrect downstream actions. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Copilot consumes Dexter-generated files as ground truth, unverified errors can propagate.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits based on Dexter output, downstream code changes may encode mistakes.
mitigations: Require human review of Dexter outputs before Copilot uses them.
Insert a verification step between agents.
Limit Dexter to draft-only outputs.
Use tests or lint checks before accepting edits.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter handles financial and market data and requests multiple third-party API keys, while Copilot sends context to GitHub’s service and is closed-source. If regulated financial or confidential data is placed into Copilot-visible buffers, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is entered into Copilot-visible context, compliance review is required.
IF organizational policy forbids third-party processing of that data class, the pair violates policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot context.
Use a policy-approved redaction step before sharing files.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repositories.
Document retention and residency expectations for both tools.
requires-engineering: perform a formal DPIA or vendor review.
